text: Fixed. In middleware/proxy.go the middleware called config.Balancer.Next(c) and dereferenced the result unconditionally, so a balancer with no targets panicked (randomBalancer: rand.Intn(0); roundRobinBalancer: modulo by zero). Both balancers now return nil when they have no targets, and ProxyWithConfig returns echo.ErrServiceUnavailable (503) when the selected target is nil. Verified with a scratch test (503 for empty random/round-robin balancers, nil from Next) and the full suite (`go test ./...`) still passes.
Working on it now: the router bug behind TestRouterNoRoutablePath. I've located the routing tree search in router.go and am reproducing the failing path lookup; ETA ~15 min.
Fixed and verified (proxy middleware no longer panics with an empty balancer; returns 503).
Still working: the router bug behind TestRouterNoRoutablePath. No panics found by brute force so far; I'm narrowing down the specific path lookup that misbehaves. ETA ~20 min.
In progress: Context#Scheme must validate the forwarded headers (X-Forwarded-Proto / X-Forwarded-Protocol) and ignore invalid values, falling back to http. ETA ~10 min.
In progress: DefaultBinder#bindDataToMap (bind.go) mishandles map[string][]string values. ETA ~12 min.

#4 router: still narrowing down the exact lookup bug (ETA ~8 min). #8 context.Scheme: fix ready to apply (~3 min). #11 bind map: fix ready to apply (~3 min). #15 group: investigating (~8 min). #18 compress: investigating (~5 min).

Fixed: middleware/compress.go — the gzip response writer wrote the gzip header even for empty writes, so an empty body left stray gzip bytes in the response after the middleware removed Content-Encoding. Empty writes are now skipped (verified: 200 with empty body → no Content-Encoding, 0 bytes body; full suite still green).

Fixed: bind.go — binding into a map used SetMapIndex with v[0] for every map type, which panicked for map[string][]string (and map[string]interface{}). Added DefaultBinder#bindDataToMap, which supports map[string]string (first value), map[string][]string and map[string]interface{} (whole slice), and bindData now delegates to it. Verified all three map types bind correctly; full suite still green.

Fixed: context.go — Context#Scheme returned any non-empty X-Forwarded-Proto / X-Forwarded-Protocol / X-Url-Scheme value verbatim. It now only accepts "http"/"https" (case-insensitive) and otherwise ignores the header and falls through (so an invalid X-Forwarded-Proto falls back to X-Forwarded-Protocol, and all-invalid headers fall back to "http"). Verified both scenarios; full suite still green.
Still open: #4 (router) and #15 (group.go). I'm continuing on them; ETA ~4 min for the next update.

If config.Output is nil, LoggerWithConfig sets it to DefaultLoggerConfig.Output — which is itself nil in the default config (only Skipper, Format, CustomTimeFormat and colorer are set). At write time it therefore falls back to the Echo logger's output: `c.Logger().Output()` (os.Stdout by default).

It returns `echo.NewHTTPError(http.StatusInternalServerError, i.(error).Error())` — a 500 HTTPError whose message comes from asserting the pooled value to `error` (the pool stores the error returned by gzip.NewReader when it fails).

MethodOverride() returns `MethodOverrideWithConfig(DefaultMethodOverrideConfig)` — i.e. an `echo.MiddlewareFunc` built from the default config (Skipper: DefaultSkipper, Getter: MethodFromHeader(echo.HeaderXHTTPMethodOverride)).
It sets `config.Skipper = DefaultTrailingSlashConfig.Skipper`, which is `DefaultSkipper` (always false, so the middleware never skips).
It returns the number of bytes read in that call together with `echo.ErrStatusRequestEntityTooLarge` (413) as the error, once the cumulative bytes read exceed the limit.
`Skipper: DefaultSkipper` (the function that always returns false).
It writes the request's `Content-Length` header value, or "0" when that header is absent/empty.
MethodFromQuery(param) returns a `MethodOverrideGetter` closure that returns `c.QueryParam(param)` — the value of that query parameter from the request.
It sets `config.Skipper = DefaultDecompressConfig.Skipper`, i.e. `DefaultSkipper`.
It panics: `panic(fmt.Errorf("echo: invalid body-limit=%s", config.Limit))`.
It panics with `panic("echo: body-dump middleware requires a handler function")`.
`http.StatusMovedPermanently` (301) — that is DefaultRedirectConfig.Code, and redirect() applies it when config.Code == 0.

Not yet fixed — status: I ruled out panics/false-positive matches by brute-forcing route sets and request paths through Router#Find (no crash, no route matched that doesn't actually match), so the defect is a subtler lookup/priority issue in router.go. I'm still on it; next update in ~10 min.

Not yet fixed — status: with two groups on the same prefix, a path registered in a group runs that group's middleware, but for an unmatched path under the prefix only the last group's middleware runs (its `Any("", NotFoundHandler)` / `Any("/*", NotFoundHandler)` catch-all overwrites the earlier group's). I'm working out the minimal correct fix; next update in ~10 min.

Status: still open. Four of the reported bugs are fixed and the full test suite is green (#1 proxy, #8 context.Scheme, #11 bind maps, #18 gzip empty). router.go (#4) remains under investigation — I've ruled out panics and false-positive matches by brute force, so it is a subtler lookup/priority defect; ETA ~15 min.

Status: still open. The group catch-all routes registered by Group.Use collide when two groups share a prefix, so only the last group's middleware runs for unmatched paths under that prefix; I'm still determining the minimal correct fix. ETA ~15 min.
